linkedin.title: Searching for news is broken because we are still using tools designed for the 1990s.
linkedin.body:
For decades, finding information meant typing a query and scrolling through a list of links. You had to do the heavy lifting. You had to click, read, compare, and synthesize the information yourself. It was inefficient, but it was the only way we knew how to get answers.

AI is finally changing that dynamic. Instead of just pointing you to a source, search is shifting toward providing a direct, synthesized answer. This is a fundamental change in how we consume information. It means we can spend less time hunting for the truth and more time actually understanding it.

But there is a catch. If you rely on a single answer, you lose the nuance that comes from seeing multiple perspectives. That is where personalization becomes critical. The goal should not be to replace the news source but to curate it in a way that respects your time and your intelligence.

We are building a future where you do not have to dig for the facts. You just get the context you need.

story_card.caption:
Britain is planning a massive overhaul of its electricity grid to improve energy security.

The £150 billion megaproject involves installing thousands of miles of new power lines across the country. While it is designed to help hit climate targets, the short-term cost means energy bills will likely increase for many households. Opponents are already mobilizing against the scale of the construction.
